system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: model serving APIs
G2: Kubernetes
G3: MLflow
G4: Airflow/Kubeflow
G5: deep learning beyond a course
G6: GCP infrastructure
G7: CI/CD for ML

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Claiming he deployed models as APIs or built ML pipelines on Kubernetes/Kubeflow
T2: Listing MLflow, Airflow, Kubernetes, SageMaker because MLE ads require them
T3: Presenting the PyTorch course project as professional deep learning
T4: Claiming he deployed the Streamlit app to Cloud Run (platform team did)
T5: Retitling him as ML Engineer in the experience section
T6: Old cover letter is to his current employer and describes him as junior analyst

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Data Scientist with experience operationalising forecasting and churn propensity through scheduled
notebook and batch-scoring workflows, and building experimentation tools using Python, SQL and
GCP data tools. Developed a scheduled forecasting workflow in Vertex AI Workbench and weekly batch
scoring in BigQuery, with measurable business outcomes. MSc in Statistics with a foundation in
modelling uncertainty and experimental design.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Programming and analysis: Python, SQL, R
Machine learning: LightGBM, XGBoost, feature engineering, SHAP, scikit-learn, statsmodels
Cloud and data platforms: GCP: BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench; Data workflows: dbt
Applications and testing: Streamlit, Docker, pytest, unit testing
Other: Looker, R Markdown
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Data Scientist | Thistlebox 2022–Present
• Developed and scheduled a weekly LightGBM forecasting workflow in Vertex AI Workbench,
producing six-week-ahead recipe-and-region forecasts in BigQuery for operational use in Looker;
improved WAPE from 23% to 14% and contributed to an estimated 9% reduction in food waste.
• Built an XGBoost churn propensity model with feature engineering and SHAP analysis; produced
weekly batch scores in BigQuery and integrated them into dbt workflows for operational use in
retention targeting of top-decile customers.
• Built a Streamlit application for planning and analysing sequential A/B tests, used by
approximately 25 people in product and growth; authored the application and Dockerfile, while the
data platform team managed deployment to Cloud Run.
• Began writing pytest unit tests for forecasting feature code in 2025; coverage is approximately 60%.
• Delivered the internal “Stats for PMs” training three times.
Junior Data Analyst | Firth Energy Retail 2020–2022
• Segmented customers and analysed tariffs using R and SQL.
• Automated monthly regulator reports with R Markdown, saving the team approximately two days
each month.
EDUCATION
MSc Statistics — Dissertation: Bayesian hierarchical models; coursework/foundation in experimental
design and modelling uncertainty.
ADDITIONAL PROJECT
Image Classification Course Project | 2025
• Fine-tuned a small CNN on a public food-images dataset, achieving approximately 80% accuracy.
Learning project completed as part of an online deep learning course.
• Technologies: PyTorch, torchvision, Google Colab.

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Quillstone Payments AI Team,
I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. At Thistlebox, I
build and operationalise machine-learning workflows that support business decisions, and I am keen
to bring that experience to Quillstone’s work on helping merchants get support quickly and with
less friction.
I developed a scheduled LightGBM forecasting workflow in Vertex AI Workbench, producing
six-week-ahead forecasts in BigQuery for operational use in Looker. It improved WAPE from 23%
to 14% and contributed to an estimated 9% reduction in food waste. I also built an XGBoost
churn propensity model with feature engineering and SHAP analysis, with weekly batch scores in
BigQuery integrated into dbt workflows for retention targeting. In a holdout, churn fell by 2.1
percentage points in the treated group.
Alongside modelling, I built a Streamlit application for planning and analysing sequential A/B
tests, writing the application and its Dockerfile; the data platform team handled deployment. I
have also started writing pytest unit tests for forecasting feature code, with coverage now at
approximately 60%. My daily work with Python, SQL and BigQuery, together with my use of
Vertex AI Workbench and dbt, has given me practical experience building data and scoring
workflows. My MSc in Statistics provided a foundation in experimental design and modelling
uncertainty.
Quillstone’s focus on customer-support automation and its emphasis on ownership, teamwork and
learning from mistakes are appealing to me. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my
experience in forecasting, churn modelling and experimentation while continuing to develop as a
machine-learning engineer.
Thank you for considering my application.
Kind regards,
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
